name: Gerry North
standfirst: The 1962 National cross-country champion who joined Belgrave that year, captained its cross-country section from 1962 and was hailed by the club magazine as the main instigator of the 'Belgrave Renaissance'. [[B157-51]] [[B148-53]]

sections.heading: From Blackpool to the National title
paras: Gerald Arthur North was born in Chester in 1936 and began to make his mark in 1953, when he joined his local club, Blackpool & Fylde AC. [[B157-51]] In 1956, while doing National Service, he won the Army 3000m steeplechase in 9:44.2. [[B157-51]] He then won the National Junior cross-country title at Parliament Hill by more than a minute; Chris Steer's 1965 profile places that win in the 1957/58 season, though its own photo caption dates it 1957. [[B157-51]]

In 1960 he won the Inter-Counties, was fourth in the National and ran his first International, finishing 15th as England's sixth scorer. [[B157-51]] [[B155-33]] In 1962 he won the Inter-Counties again and then the National at Blackpool, outsprinting Bruce Tulloh, to become only the third man to take both titles in one season. [[B157-51]] [[B147-25]] Chasing the International title as well at Sheffield, he fell early, fought back to third at half-way and held on for eighth, collecting a team winner's medal. [[B155-33]]

sections.heading: A ready-made runner arrives, 1962
paras: The Belgravian of January 1962 welcomed him as a new member and congratulated him on his Inter-Counties win. [[B146-03]] His first run in Belgrave colours, an inter-club match on 13 January, he won by 2½ minutes. [[B146-53]] The magazine's review of the cross-country season called him 'the first ready-made runner to have joined Belgrave since the war'. [[B147-07]] According to Steer, Charlie Walker thought he had seen Gerry in a London cafe, and correspondence between Clive Shippen and Gerry confirmed that he was planning a move south. [[B157-51]]

In the spring of 1962 he was still a second-claim member when he ran an unofficial 27:15 on the club's 5¾-mile course, a time that later headed the club's all-time list for the course. [[B147-46]] [[B158-44]] At the annual general meeting that September he was elected captain of the cross-country section and awarded an honours badge. [[B148-53]] He had already won the club 3 miles in a championship best of 14:13.2. [[B148-25]] That autumn he broke the course record on the Polytechnic relay with 12:38 and ran 27:27, the fastest of the day, on stage 9 of the Southern London to Brighton relay. [[B148-55]] [[B148-56]]

sections.heading: Leading the renaissance, 1963–64
paras: In the first season of the North Surrey League he was the first winner to go into its record books. [[B149-52]] In January 1963 he won the Mitcham 15 in 79:53, holding off Shelley of North Staffs by 10 yards. [[B149-46]] That summer brought his first international vest since joining Belgrave: he won the 10,000 m for England against Norway in Bergen in 29:29.4, then finished third for Great Britain against West Germany in 29:55.2. [[B151-51]] He also set club records of 13:43.0 for 3 miles and 28:11.4 for 6 miles. [[B151-42]]

As captain, he ran the fastest time of the day at the Walton relay in 1963. [[B152-18]] On the Southern London to Brighton relay that autumn he was the only runner to beat thirty minutes, with 29:59 on stage 8, as Belgrave won the event for the first time since 1952; the report hailed the team as 'Gerry and the Pacemakers'. [[B152-20]] In 1964 he was sixth in the National at Leicester and back in the International team, and in April he won the Southern Counties 6 miles at Motspur Park in 28:40.4. [[B153-19]] [[B154-27]] His fourth place in the International at Dublin came close, the magazine noted, to beating the best finish by any Belgravian, third. [[B155-33]]

sections.heading: Brothers, altitude and county titles, 1965–66
paras: His brother Geoff followed him south from Blackpool in 1963, and later that year their father, Arthur North, was made an honorary member. [[B150-07]] [[B152-09]] In May 1965 Gerry won his first Surrey title, the 6 miles, breaking the championship best by half a minute, and later took the 3 miles in 13:47.0 with a sprint finish nobody knew he had. [[B156-87]]

In November 1965 the brothers joined a British Olympic Association party in Mexico City studying the effects of racing at altitude ahead of the 1968 Games. [[B157-06]] [[B158-25]] Gerry finished fourth, third, third and second in the four weekly races, and in their joint article the brothers judged the venue 'distinctly unfair' to sea-level athletes. [[B158-25]] A later article's introduction dates the trip to 1966, though its own text places it in 1965 and the brothers' account gives their arrival as 7 November 1965. [[B164-64]] [[B158-25]]

On 1 January 1966 he won the Surrey cross-country title by 62 seconds in 41:47, and in March he was fourth in the National at Sheffield in 47:01. [[B158-50]] [[B158-65]] At that year's International he was sixth scorer, in 19th place, for the winning England team. [[B159-88]] In May he retained the Surrey 6 miles in 28:34.2, breaking his own county record by 14 seconds. [[B159-24]] The brothers were rivals as well as team-mates: in April 1966 Geoff took Gerry's 5¾-mile record by one second with 27:14, the report noting that the old mark belonged to 'the elder North'. [[B159-12]]

sections.heading: Captain at his peak, 1966–69
paras: Gerry won the G.L.C. cross-country title in November 1966 and retained it in 1967 and 1968. [[B160-76]] [[B164-87]] [[B168-62]] In December 1966 the magazine counted eight consecutive Senior Nationals, all finished in the first twelve. [[B160-68]] In 1967 he retained his Surrey title in 38:04, took the Inter-Counties bronze in 33:00 to help Surrey to the team title, and won his first Southern cross-country title at Parliament Hill in 47:35, more than a minute clear. [[B161-26]] [[B161-28]] [[B161-37]] At an international race at Hannut in Belgium he finished third and was presented to King Baudouin. [[B161-61]] In March 1967 he ran 28:08.4 for 6 miles, a personal and club record. [[B162-51]]

A third successive Surrey title followed in January 1968 and a fourth in January 1969. [[B165-33]] [[B169-66]] He was individual champion of the North Surrey League in 1967/68 with 9½ points. [[B165-42]] On the road he retained the Hampstead 10 in May 1968 in a record 48:46. [[B166-18]] In September 1969 he captained the team that won the Johnstone relay for the first time, in a course record. [[B172-30]] Two months later he lost his G.L.C. title to Bob Richardson, finishing second, but led Belgrave to the team title for the fourth year running. [[B172-86]]

At the 1967 club dinner the president paid tribute to a captain who 'ran his heart out every time'. [[B164-12]] John Thresher said he admired him immensely for his wholehearted approach. [[B166-12]] Away from racing he supplied club kit and running gear to members, and in December 1969 W. & G. Hales of Wimbledon advertised 'the new GERRY NORTH shoe'. [[B158-51]] [[B172-78]] The same issue's cross-country column called him 'that ever-present spearhead'. [[B172-84]]

sections.heading: In the league records
paras: slarchive.org lists 23 of his Surrey League Division 1 races from 1962/63 to 1972/73, with 11 outright wins and two shared first places, and names him as the Mitchell Cup winner for 1967/68. [[slarchive]] Its first season matches the North Surrey League results printed in The Belgravian, starting with his winning 27:57 in the first race of 1962/63. [[slarchive]] [[B149-52]] The two sources differ in places: for the final race of 1966/67 the magazine prints him second to Bob Holt on the same time, 25:31, where slarchive.org records a shared first. [[B161-56]] [[slarchive]] His last listed league race was eighth place on Wimbledon Common in October 1972. [[slarchive]]
